outcome: side effects (palpitation, tachycardia, bradycardia, headache, oliguria, dizziness, muscle cramps, nasal congestion)
cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women with severe hypertension (systolic BP >= 160 mm Hg or diastolic BP >= 110 mm Hg) at 34 weeks of gestation or more, with or without proteinuria, who were either in labor or not.
finding: Both intravenous labetalol and intravenous hydralazine were comparable in antihypertensive efficacy for managing hypertensive emergency in pregnancy, though hydralazine had more side effects mimicking pre-eclampsia, and labetalol raised concerns about neonatal bradycardia.
